quick.summary: How to keep your work list small and ready.
quick.takeaway: Delete old items to make room for fresh ideas.

beats.line: We spent an hour reading old requests today. Why is the list so useless?
Think of your fridge. If you never throw food out, it smells bad.
So my work list is full of rotten food.
Exactly. Good ideas expire. Needs change over time.
We call this regular cleanup backlog refinement.
Can I just say clean the fridge?
You can. Delete what is old and stale.
Keep the top items small and ready. Leave the bottom vague.
I will delete anything we ignored for six months.
Now your team has room for fresh ideas.

quiz.question: When reviewing a list of very old requests, what is the best approach?
quiz.explanation: Old requests often represent expired ideas. Removing them keeps the team focused on what matters now.

quiz.question: It is a good practice to keep every idea on the backlog forever.
quiz.explanation: Treating a work list like a permanent storage bin makes it too cluttered to be useful.
